complexity.notes: Decode is quadratic due to repeated s = s[...] slicing; using an index pointer (or StringIO/pointer walk) instead of re-slicing would make it O(n). Also int(s[0:a]) and s.index('|') re-scan the header each time; encode is fine. Consider a delimiter unlikely to confuse (current scheme is actually correct since length prefix disambiguates '|' inside content).
complexity.summary: Encodes each string as 'length|content' concatenated together; decode repeatedly finds the next '|', parses the length prefix, and slices out that many characters. Because decode re-slices the remaining string on every iteration, each of the k strings triggers an O(n) copy, giving O(n*k) = O(n^2) overall.
